# Rustdoc JSON format 57 fixture

`rustdoc_v57_fixture.json` is a minimal projection of real output from Rust
1.94.0 rustdoc. The source is `lib.rs`; it exercises inherent/trait member
name collisions, required and provided trait members, a derived external-trait
implementation (rustdoc marks it `automatically_derived` and
`is_synthetic: false`), default associated type/constant values, distinct
`Contract<u8>` and `Contract<u16>` implementations, a generic owner with an
explicit `where T: Copy` predicate, concrete generic aliases, a private trait
on a public type, and enum payloads. `Fixed<u16>` also has an inherent method
used to verify that aliases filter implementations by concrete type argument.
An empty implementation of `DefaultMembers` verifies that default associated
constants and types remain visible. `GenericDerivedAlias` checks that a concrete
alias does not inherit an implementation whose `Copy` predicate it cannot meet.
Tuple-specialized inherent implementations test recursive generic argument
matching, and a public trait nested in a private module tests export reachability.
The projection also retains elided and alpha-renamed lifetime inherent
implementations for private `View` types re-exported as `Alias` and
`AlphaAlias`, an inline `T: 'static` bound, a `where 'a: 'static` lifetime
predicate, an inline `'a: 'static` lifetime parameter bound, one real synthetic
`Send` implementation, one applicable blanket `Borrow<T>` implementation, and
Rust's real blanket `Any` implementation.
These cases test re-export paths, structured handling of outlives bounds, and
concrete vs. open generic aliases without fabricated rustdoc item records. The
associated type default uses Rust's `associated_type_defaults` feature only in
this test fixture.

The source was captured with:

```text
$env:RUSTC_BOOTSTRAP = '1'
rustdoc +1.94.0 --edition 2024 --crate-name rustdoc_v57_fixture --crate-type lib --output-format json -Z unstable-options --document-private-items --document-hidden-items lib.rs --out-dir <temporary-directory>
python project_fixture.py <temporary-directory>/rustdoc_v57_fixture.json rustdoc_v57_fixture.json
```

The checked-in JSON is generated by projecting source-owned records plus the
three representative external implementation records named above. It preserves
rustdoc's actual format-57 item records and relationships while omitting
unrelated standard-library and compiler-generated implementation records to
keep the test input small. The `format_version` and `includes_private` fields
remain the original rustdoc values. Do not hand-author item shapes in this
fixture; regenerate it from the source and project the required records when
its source changes.
